content: 1. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. It is recommended to use caution, monitor closely, and consider using non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 2. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, slows gastric emptying, which can reduce the absorption and efficacy of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before or 11 hours after exenatide administration. 3. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH, which affects absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary, and monitor closely. 5. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor serum potassium levels during initiation and dosage adjustments of finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 6. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid co-administration if possible, or modify the dose of BCRP substrates. Do not exceed an ethinylestradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 10. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Ethinylestradiol increases green tea levels by decreasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hemin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may reduce the efficacy of hemin. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of ibandronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of hyaluronidase by rendering tissues partially resistant to its action. Patients may require larger amounts of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may increase plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 19. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of insulin degludec by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of insulin degludec, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 21. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Istradefylline increases the levels of norethindrone acetate and ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. At a dose of 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with a 20 mg/day dose. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 23. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as itraconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Lansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels of lamotrigine by increasing hepatic clearance, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when co-administered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 29. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of levodopa by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral administration of iron salts should be separated from levodopa by at least two hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inhibitors such as ketoconazole may increase plasma hormone levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of levothyroxine and liothyronine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by four hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 35. Lixisenatide delays gastric emptying, which may reduce the absorption of oral medications, including ethinylestradiol. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Norethindrone acetate increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lomitapide doses should not exceed 30 mg/day. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of lonapegsomatropin by reducing serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ferrous fumarate decreases the levels of methyldopa by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by inhibiting its metabolism, potentially prolonging sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ferrous fumarate and norethindrone acetate by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely.
